title: Getting Noticed Before a Word Is Spoken
coreMove: Use low-threat nonverbal cues to make the first seconds of contact feel safe enough for conversation to begin.
sourcePressure: The ch02 source centers first impressions and friend signals: eyebrow flash, head tilt, smile, and open posture reduce perceived threat before words can help. It also warns that signals open the door but do not create lasting trust alone.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating friend signals as charisma tricks that guarantee rapport without later substance.

sourceAnchors.name: eyebrow flash
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch02 sidecar identifies eyebrow flash as a rapid nonthreat signal.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A quick eyebrow flash can tell a stranger you recognize them without making them feel cornered.

sourceAnchors.name: head tilt
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says a head tilt reads as vulnerable and trusting rather than guarded.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A small head tilt softens the opening because guarded bodies rarely expose the neck by accident.

hook: Your body speaks before you do
tryThisNow: practice smiling in a mirror for one minute

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital wayfinding volunteer approaching worried visitors at a cardiac wing elevator
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer whose first move can calm or crowd a family
exampleSpecs.stakes: the family is already scared and may snap at help that feels intrusive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the volunteer stops walking straight into their path, uses an eyebrow flash from two steps away, tilts his head, and points to the desk before speaking
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the elevator doors open onto a blue cardiac-wing sign

exampleSpecs.domain: a farmers market stall owner trying to invite browsing without pouncing
exampleSpecs.audience: a first-time vendor in a crowded Saturday market
exampleSpecs.stakes: too much eagerness sends shoppers past the table
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the vendor compares crossed-arm watching with an open posture and brief smile, then sees browsers slow when the signal says safe rather than sales trap
exampleSpecs.firstImage: steam rising from a crate of apple-cider samples

exampleSpecs.domain: a probation office receptionist greeting a tense client arriving late
exampleSpecs.audience: a receptionist who controls the first emotional temperature of the room
exampleSpecs.stakes: one sharp opening could turn delay into confrontation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 9:04 a.m., Thomas chooses a visible open palm and low-threat nod before asking for the appointment card
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated appointment card bent at one corner

exampleSpecs.domain: a university lab partner joining an established research bench
exampleSpecs.audience: a student entering a group that already has routines
exampleSpecs.stakes: if the first approach feels presumptuous, collaboration starts cold
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Is this the pipette rack everyone fights over?" Camille asks after a small smile and head tilt soften the joke

exampleSpecs.domain: a cycling repair shop owner handling a customer embarrassed about a broken commuter bike
exampleSpecs.audience: a shop owner who needs approachability before advice
exampleSpecs.stakes: the customer may leave rather than admit what happened
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you notice the customer scanning for judgment, so you lower the tool, uncross your stance, and let the first cue say there is no threat here
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bent derailleur hanging above a rubber shop mat

exampleSpecs.domain: a local election canvasser approaching a porch with a wary homeowner
exampleSpecs.audience: a canvasser learning that distance and posture decide whether the door stays open
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rushed pitch will get the door closed before policy is heard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes three slammed doors for the canvasser to see that stepping back, flashing recognition, and angling his body matters before the script
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three crossed-out addresses on a clipboard

skillTargets: select a low-threat cue for a tense first contact
tell when friend signals are contradicted by later behavior
separate approachability from submission or fakery
evaluate recovery from a poor first impression

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next doorway or meeting entry, pause at two steps away, uncross your posture, give brief recognition, and let the other person respond before you close distance.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
